newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Strong buying keeps Vietnam pepper rally alive.
newsitem.headline: Strong buying keeps Vietnam pepper rally alive.

text.p: Vietnamese pepper prices continued to rise this week on strong demand and dwindling stocks from the latest harvest, traders said on Thursday.
They put the market at $3,500-3,550 per tonne, FOB Saigon Port, compared with prices of between $3,100 and 3,350 last week and about $3,000 two months ago.

Traders estimated that Vietnam has exported 17,000-20,000 tonnes of this year's pepper crop, which started at the end of January. Sales from the annual harvest, which this year is expected to be some 20,000 tonnes, usually continue until August.

"That means Vietnam is now already running out of pepper and the stock left is quite low, around 1,000 tonnes throughout the whole country", one trader said. "The (pepper export) market can continue to operate only for a couple of weeks."
The main buyers of Vietnamese pepper are from European countries, with the majority being shipped through Singapore.
Industry sources say a golden age is returning for pepper in Vietnam, which became a major exporter during a short-lived surge in world prices during the 1980s.
They said some cashew growers in the southern province of Dong Nai, one of the country's main pepper-growing areas, are cutting down their plants and replacing them with pepper instead.
"Vietnam could become a big pepper exporter in five years", one trader said, noting that was the time lag between planting a pepper tree and its first harvest.
